first_impression.reaction: My assistant pulled it up because Hawaii is on the list and she wanted to know whether the legal side would complicate anything. The first screen is calm and direct, no prices, no gushing. But it's a step-by-step legal guide for a couple doing it themselves. Her summary would be 'clear and reliable on the paperwork, nothing about scale or privacy'. I'd read the takeaways, the timing section, the beach permits and the end.

journey.quote: Getting married in Hawaii as an Australian couple is straightforward.
journey.reaction: Good. I want to hear the legal part is simple so it doesn't drive the whole plan. Short and confident, not breathless.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Australians visiting the United States for less than 90 days may be eligible to apply for an Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA) and enter under the Visa Waiver Program.
journey.reaction: Our guests come from Dubai, London and Sydney. This only speaks to Australians, and it's the sort of thing my assistant already knows. Explaining what an e-Passport is tells me the page isn't written for us.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Keep both passports with you, not in the luggage you send ahead to the villa.
journey.reaction: Small, but it reads like someone who has actually run a wedding week with luggage moving separately. That's the voice I want.

journey.section: Pick up your licence together, in person
journey.quote: You must appear together, in person. Proxies are not allowed.
journey.reaction: Useful, and blunt in the right way. Our schedules are split across three cities, so this changes how we plan arrivals.

journey.section: Timing the appointment around your arrival
journey.quote: Leave a buffer before the rehearsal and the welcome dinner, and keep the appointment away from any day with an early inter-island flight.
journey.reaction: This is planner thinking rather than a government summary. I like that it fits the legal step into a multi-day event.

journey.section: Permits for beach and outdoor ceremonies
journey.quote: Sand is public in a way a lawn is not.
journey.reaction: The most relevant line for me. If the shoreline is public, I can't close it, so a beach ceremony is out for us. I'd have liked the page to say the same thing about privacy outright, and what a private estate or exclusive-use resort changes.

journey.quote: Day length runs from about 11 hours to about 13.5 hours.
journey.reaction: Too much detail. The weather section goes on longer than I need. Just tell me which months and which coast.

journey.quote: It suits a wedding weekend built around one resort and a long evening on the terrace.
journey.reaction: Now we're talking about the event, not the forms. But one resort for 300 guests over several days raises the questions I actually have: can it be taken over completely, and who handles security?

journey.quote: The legal steps are fixed. Everything else, from the lawn to the last shuttle, is a planning decision, and it is where a Hawaii wedding becomes yours.
journey.reaction: A good line, but 'the last shuttle' gives it away. We'd be talking about private transfers and our own drivers, not shuttles.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans your venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One point of contact suits me, because fewer people means fewer leaks. 'Inclusions' sounds a little like a package, though.

journey.section: Plan your Hawaii wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee agreed in writing is reassuring for my family office. Quoting in AUD and 'your time zone' assume I'm sitting in Sydney.

unanswered_questions: Have you planned a Hawaii wedding for 200 to 400 guests, and can you show me one discreetly? (deferred business detail)
How is the Wedded Advisor fee worked out, and do you earn commission from the resorts you book? (deferred business detail)
Who would actually be on the ground in Hawaii for us during the wedding week? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange private transfers and inter-island charters for guests? (deferred business detail)
What access or perks come with booking through you, such as Wedded Privileges? (deferred business detail)
Will you handle the licence appointment and officiant paperwork for us, or is it 'yours to collect' as the page says? (deferred business detail)
Can a resort or estate in Hawaii be taken over exclusively for several days, and can our own security work with theirs?
How do you handle confidentiality: NDAs, guest lists, no social media?
Can I work through my assistant or family office, and can you quote in another currency?

turn_offs_found.quote: To use the Visa Waiver Program you need an e-Passport, a passport with an embedded electronic chip, marked by the international symbol on the cover.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. Telling me what an e-Passport looks like makes the page feel aimed at a first-time traveller, not at someone who'd hire a premium planner.

turn_offs_found.quote: Everything else, from the lawn to the last shuttle, is a planning decision, and it is where a Hawaii wedding becomes yours.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Shuttle' is group-tour language. It's minor, but it's in the one section about the planning, so it shapes how I picture the service.

would_share_with: My assistant might keep the licence timing section for the planning file. Nobody else.

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start a conversation with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=getting-married-in-hawaii&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I don't enquire through a public link on a blog post. I'd want a private introduction and some sign you've done this at our size and keep it quiet. The paperwork advice is solid, but nothing here speaks to exclusive use, security or discretion.

top_3_changes: In 'Permits for beach and outdoor ceremonies', follow 'Ceremonies on resort or private grounds are a different matter.' with one line of generic advice: ask whether the venue can offer exclusive use or close the ceremony space to the public, and how its security works with a private team. Write it as a question to ask, not a claim about Wedded Wonderland.
Replace 'the last shuttle' in 'Venues and planning' with something neutral like 'the last transfer', so the planning section doesn't sound like a group tour.
Trim the e-Passport explanation and the day-length sentence so the page explains less and reads as more assured.
